rich_narrative.summary: Intercultural Networks, Inc. (ING) is a faith-based organization that provides seminars and training to promote understanding across different communities and <cite id="1">counter bigotry through education</cite>. Founded in <cite id="2">1993</cite>, the organization operates primarily in the United States, focusing on <cite id="3">intercultural dialogue and DEI training</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="4">total revenue of $688,262</cite>, representing a <cite id="5">3-year revenue growth rate of 10.7%</cite>. Despite its long history, the organization faces significant financial efficiency challenges. In FY2023, the <cite id="6">program expense ratio was 39.5%</cite>, which is substantially below the <cite id="7">75% industry standard</cite> and the <cite id="8">97% peer median</cite> for similar religious and cultural groups. This indicates that a majority of funds are directed toward administrative and fundraising costs rather than direct service delivery. While the organization maintains <cite id="9">5.2 months of working capital</cite> for short-term stability, its <cite id="10">board of directors consists of only one member</cite>, which limits independent oversight and governance capacity.
